plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win, while bidding lower reduces my chances of winning without changing what I'd pay. Since my value is $32, I should bid exactly $32 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this setup, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $6, I should bid exactly $6 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In such auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price above my value (negative profit). If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $17.
